transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~54 minutes | Attendees: Olivia, Marcus, Sofia (Redwood); Daniel, Leah, Tom, Priya (Aurora)

Summary: quick renewal and expansion check to discuss capacity upgrades (more GPUs, committed tiers), opening additional regions (EU), contract extension cadence and outstanding security docs. Customer wants predictable cost for Q1-2026 ramps plus EU data residency for EU customers.

[00:00] Olivia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll keep this tight. I'm Olivia, AE on the account, with Marcus our SE and Sofia on CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Daniel: Hey, good thanks. Busy, lots of infra stuff, but good.
[00:15] Leah: Hi all. We're focused on the Q1 ramp so want to lock in capacity.
[00:20] Tom: Tom from procurement, I'll be listening in.
[00:25] Priya: Priya, security. I'll mostly ask about audits and encryption.
[00:35] Olivia: Great. Goal today is quick recap of current usage, walk through expansion asks — Daniel mentioned EU region, higher committed capacity and a one year extension — and align on next steps. Marcus, want to kick to usage and technical constraints?
[00:50] Marcus: Sure. Quick recap: Aurora is on Dedicated with a three-pool setup, currently 12 GPUs reserved across two zones in us-east-1, plus burst to on-demand when spikes hit. Typical p95 generation latency is ~110ms for most of your short-form chat traffic, tail bursts around 450ms when KV cache misses happen. Leah, you shared the token profile earlier — majority of calls are <512 tokens, but you have a 5% long-tail at 2k tokens which is driving KV pressure.
[01:20] Leah: Yep that's right. We're fine on most days, but during settlement windows latency spikes matter. We want a predictable floor and to not surprise the ops team with spikes in cost.
[01:35] Daniel: Also regulatory ask — for EU customers we need data residency and lower latency to EU markets. So adding eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 is priority.
[01:50] Marcus: Totally doable. Two options: spin up a Dedicated pool in EU (reserved capacity) or use Hosted with a strict regional routing policy. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput/SLO and isolated capacity; hosted is faster to launch but has multi-tenant characteristics and different SLAs. For financial workloads I'd recommend Dedicated in eu-west-1 with VPC peering.
[02:15] Priya: On security, we'll need SOC 2 Type II, encryption at rest with our KMS (we use Azure Key Vault), SAML SSO, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Can you confirm Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and log forwarding?
[02:35] Sofia: Yes — we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations and can forward audit logs; I'll attach our security pack after the call. The SOC 2 report is available.
[02:50] Priya: Okay, please send. We also need answers on data retention hooks — can we set retention to 30 days for logs?
[03:00] Marcus: Yes we can configure retention. There are a few nuances around prefix caching and ephemeral KV entries but we can set policies for transcripts and logs.
[03:15] Tom: From procurement, we need pricing tiers for committed spend and burst allowances. Last time the billing looked a little unpredictable when bursts kicked in. We need an easier model for internal approvals.
[03:30] Olivia: Understood. We can propose three commitment tiers — small, medium, large — with burst buffers and price protections. We'll detail unit economics (per-token plus reserved GPU cost). I'll send a concrete proposal.
[03:45] Daniel: Can you also include an option for a 12-month contract with a 6-month review clause? We want to commit but retain a chance to expand earlier if our usage grows faster.
[03:55] Olivia: Yes, we can add review milestones and a bump schedule.

[04:15] Marcus: One technical note — if you move to an EU Dedicated pool, we recommend enabling more aggressive prefix/KV caching for your settlement workflows to reduce token throughput during the heavy tail. Also consider quantized model variants for some low-risk routes to save cost.
[04:35] Leah: Quantized variants — are there regressions in accuracy we should expect?
[04:40] Marcus: Small ones, mostly on edge cases. We can run prompt-preserving evals against a customer prompt set to validate. We also recommend canarying model variants.
[04:55] Leah: Okay that sounds fine if we can test.

[05:10] Priya: Back to compliance — what's the process for an on-prem or private deployment? If some EU data must remain within our VPC, is Redwood Private an option?
[05:25] Olivia: Redwood Private is an option for regulated workloads. It requires a private control plane and typically enterprise licensing. For most customers Dedicated in region with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS suffices, but if you need full air-gap we'll bring in the Private offering. Sofia can follow up on the product differences with a short doc.
[05:45] Sofia: I'll share a comparison doc — dedicated vs private vs hosted — with key tradeoffs.

[06:00] Marcus: Another operational thing: autoscaling policy. Right now you have manual scale steps. We can propose an autoscale policy that scales by thresholding on queue depth and p95 latency to avoid surprises. That helps with cost predictability too.
[06:15] Daniel: We like that. Can it be bounded so procurement knows the max spend?
[06:20] Marcus: Yes, you can set hard caps and burst quotas. We'll include recommended caps in the proposal.

[06:40] Tom: On the contract extension: target is to extend for 12 months starting 2026-01-01. We need final numbers by end of November to get internal approvals.
[06:55] Olivia: Great — timeline is doable. We'll send the committed capacity options this week.

[07:10] Daniel: For EU testing, we'd like Redwood to run benchmarks using our test script and synthetic traffic to measure p95 and throughput in eu-west-1. Can Redwood run that or do we run it ourselves?
[07:25] Marcus: We can run both. If you share the script and credentials for a test host we can execute and send raw logs; or we can share a standard test harness we use for customers. For the Dedicated pool we'll provision a small test capacity and run the tests.
[07:40] Leah: We'll share the script. Ideally we want numbers with KV cache warm and cold to see real worst-case.
[07:50] Marcus: Noted — we'll run warm and cold runs and include KV miss rates.

[08:10] Olivia: Any blockers from security for proceeding with a regional Dedicated pilot?
[08:15] Priya: Not blockers, just documentation. We'll need the SOC 2 report, architecture diagram showing VPC peering, and proof of KMS integration. Also questions about who can access raw request logs inside Redwood.
[08:30] Sofia: Access is limited — role-based access controls, and we can provide audit logs showing who accessed what. I'll include an anonymized audit log sample.
[08:45] Priya: Good. Also want contractual language around breach notification timeline and subprocessor list.
[08:55] Olivia: We'll loop in legal to adjust the DPA and include the requested clauses.

[09:15] Marcus: Quick aside on latency targets: for eu-west-1 Dedicated we expect p95 in the 90-140ms range for your typical token lengths, depending on model variant. If you need lower 50ms p95, that's a different cost profile and we'd discuss edge caching or smaller local model sizes.
[09:40] Daniel: 90-140ms is acceptable; lower would be nice but not required.

[10:00] Tom: Pricing question — can you give an example of how committed GPU pool pricing compares to on-demand hourly plus token charges? We need a clear table.
[10:15] Olivia: Yes, we'll include a table showing effective per-token cost under each tier. In broad strokes reserved capacity buys you predictability and a discount of 20-35% vs pure on-demand depending on term and volume. Burst usage would be billed at on-demand but with a cap in the agreement.
[10:40] Leah: For expansion, can we add capacity mid-contract? We may need to add 6-8 GPUs quickly next quarter.
[10:50] Olivia: Absolutely, you can add capacity. We can include an expansion clause to scale pools with a notice period (e.g., 7-14 days) and pro-rated billing.

[11:10] Marcus: For the EU pilot, we'll propose a minimal Dedicated pool (4 GPUs) for testing latency and throughput. If that passes, we can scale to the requested 12 GPUs.
[11:25] Daniel: Let's do that. We want the pilot to show both latency and cost delta vs hosted EU routing.
[11:35] Marcus: We'll capture that. Also will run quantization experiments to show cost savings vs accuracy delta.

[12:00] Priya: On encryption — does Redwood support bring-your-own-key with Azure Key Vault?
[12:05] Marcus: Yes, we have integrations with major KMS providers including Azure Key Vault; keys can be customer-managed.
[12:12] Priya: Okay we'll need a technical runbook for setting it up.
[12:17] Sofia: We'll provide a runbook and a checklist.

[12:30] Olivia: Quick recap and timeline: action items include the committed capacity proposal, security pack, EU benchmark and procurement timeline. Questions?
[12:40] Leah: No further questions.
[12:45] Daniel: One ask — can we try a 30-day retention for logs and transcripts? If that's configurable we'll opt for that.
[12:55] Marcus: Configurable, yes. We'll document default and options.

[13:10] Tom: Procurement will also need a term sheet and PO process. If you can share a standard term sheet that lists cancellations and SLAs that helps.
[13:20] Olivia: We'll include a term sheet in the packet.

[13:35] Sofia: I'll follow up with the security pack and attach the SOC 2 summary and audit log sample by Friday.
[13:45] Olivia: And Marcus will run the EU benchmark and send results next week.
[13:50] Leah: Thank you.
[13:55] Priya: Thanks.
[14:00] Olivia: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene week of 2025-11-24 to finalize. Bye.

Post-call notes: brief crosstalk around exact GPU types (A100 vs H100) — customer prefers H100 for HPC-like loads; Redwood to confirm availability and price delta in proposal. Transcription may have misattributed a couple of lines (Speaker labels auto-generated).
